segments.text: What if your kidney stone could be removed... without a single cut on your body?
Doctor Bikramjit Singh Sodhi, Consultant Urologist, explains R.I.R.S. Retrograde Intrarenal Surgery.
A thin, flexible camera travels through the natural urinary passage, all the way up into the kidney. No cut outside.
Then, a laser breaks the stone into tiny fragments, and fine dust.
Some fragments are removed during surgery. The finer dust passes out with urine, over the following days or weeks.
A D.J. stent may be placed, to help drainage and healing. It is usually removed after a few weeks.
But here is what many patients don't know. A large stone may not clear in one sitting.
Depending on its size, location, hardness, and your kidney's anatomy, some patients need two, or even three sittings.
This is called staged R.I.R.S. An accepted approach in selected patients. Your urologist may also plan a second-look procedure, to remove any remaining fragments.
The goal is safe, effective stone clearance.
For the right treatment of your kidney stones, consult your urologist.
